He played [[college basketball]] player for the [[NJIT Highlanders men's basketball|NJIT Highlanders]], [[UTEP Miners men's basketball|UTEP Miners]] and [[Coppin State Eagles men's basketball|Coppin State Eagles]]. He was named the [[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|MEAC Player of the Year]] for the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]]. ==College career== Tarke attended [[Gaithersburg High School]] and was named to the All-Met team by the ''[[Washington Post]]''. After a prep season at Coastal Academy in New Jersey, he committed to play college basketball at the [[New Jersey Institute of Technology]] (NJIT).{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Ashley|title=Third School's The Charm For Coppin State Men's Basketball's Anthony Tarke|url=https://pressboxonline.com/2020/12/14/third-schools-the-charm-for-coppin-state-mens-basketballs-anthony-tarke/|work=pressboxonline.com|date=December 14, 2020|access-date=March 5, 2021}} He had a successful start to his career, averaging 9.9 points and 4.7 rebounds per game, earning [[ASUN Conference]] all-freshman team honors. He followed this up by moving full time into the [[NJIT Highlanders men's basketball|Highlanders]]' starting lineup, improving his averages to 15.7 points and 6.2 rebounds per game and was named to the first-team All-Atlantic Sun. Following this season, Tarke decided to transfer to a program that would provide a higher level of competition, choosing the [[University of Texas at El Paso]] (UTEP). After sitting out the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19 season]], he played one season for the [[UTEP Miners men's basketball|Miners]], but found playing time inconsistent. He chose to enter the transfer portal again, this time as an immediately-eligible graduate transfer.{{cite web|first=Adrian|last=Broaddus|title=Anthony Tarke becomes the latest Miner to enter the transfer portal|url=https://krod.com/anthony-tarke-becomes-latest-miner-to-enter-the-transfer-portal/|work=krod.com|date=March 25, 2020|access-date=March 5, 2021}} Tarke chose [[Coppin State Eagles men's basketball|Coppin State]] and head coach [[Juan Dixon]] for his final year of eligibility. On the season, he averaged 16.4 points, 8.4 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game for the Eagles, who went on to win a share of the [[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference|MEAC]] North division regular season title. At the close of the season, Tarke was named the [[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|MEAC Player of the Year]] and Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite press release|url=https://meacsports.com/news/2021/3/5/meac-announces-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors-presented-by-townebank.aspx|title=MEAC Announces Men's Basketball All-Conference Honors, presented by TowneBank|publisher=[[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference]] |date=March 5, 2021 |access-date=March 5, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Motor City Cruise (2021–2022)=== After going undrafted in the
